## ServiceSettings v0.2.0

This release replaces the Electron runtime with **Tauri 2**. Nothing in the UI changed: the same cards, the same switches, the same hover-to-delete delay, and the same messages. What changed is everything between a card and `sc.exe` / `net.exe`.

### What stayed the same

- The command layer still runs a fixed executable with an argv array — never a shell string — and rejects any service name outside `^[\w.$-]+$`.
- `sc query` stays elevation-free; `start` / `stop` still require administrator rights and still return 「权限不足，请以管理员身份重新启动本程序」 when they don't have them.
- Console output is still GBK-decoded on Chinese Windows, commands still time out after 20 s, still run without a console window, and `4  RUNNING` is still the only state counted as running.
- Elevation is still checked once at startup with at most one UAC prompt; declining it still leaves the window usable.
- Cards are still stored in IndexedDB (`TestDB` / `config` / id `1`), and the return shape of a service command is still `{ success, running?, message? }`.

### What changed

- **Backend**: the Electron main process, preload bridge and `ipcMain` handler are gone. `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` now owns validation, process execution, decoding, timeouts, elevation checks (`TokenElevation`) and the `runas` self-relaunch. The renderer calls `invoke('service_command', { action, name })` through `src/renderer/src/api.js`.
- **Validation is now enforced in two places.** In v0.1.3 the main process and the renderer shared one `src/shared/services.js`. A Tauri frontend can call `invoke` directly, so the whitelist and regex now live in Rust as the actual security boundary; `SERVICE_NAME_PATTERN` in the renderer is only an input hint. Both sides carry a comment requiring the rules to stay in sync.
- **Platform support is explicit.** The Windows NSIS build is the only target. On other platforms the service command returns an 「不支持此平台」 error instead of a misleading permission error.
- **Smaller footprint**: no bundled Chromium or Node runtime; the WebView2 runtime is used instead (bundled with Windows 11, bootstrapped on Windows 10).
- The `<meta>` CSP in `index.html` was removed — Tauri injects the CSP via `tauri.conf.json` (`app.security.csp`), and a meta CSP would be intersected with it and block IPC.

### Before you upgrade

**The service list does not carry over.** v0.1.x stored cards in an Electron Chromium profile; v0.2.0 stores them in the WebView2 profile under `com.makabakax.service-settings`. The database schema is unchanged, but the two runtimes use different directories, so after upgrading you will see the first-run `mysql` placeholder again. Add your services once more; from this release onward the list persists normally.

### Build requirements

Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`, Rust stable, MSVC Build Tools / Windows SDK, and the WebView2 Runtime (only for running the app; the NSIS installer bootstraps it when missing).
